newsitem.title: POLAND: FERGIE, ANDY HAPPY IN SINGLE LIVES UNDER ONE ROOF.
newsitem.headline: FERGIE, ANDY HAPPY IN SINGLE LIVES UNDER ONE ROOF.

text.p: The Duchess of York and her ex-husband Prince Andrew are happy leading single lives under the same roof two months after she moved back into the marital home, she told a news conference in Warsaw on Monday.

"It may be very extraordinary to most people but we manage to retain our independent single lives while living under the same roof," the Duchess, known in Britain by the nickname Fergie, said after being asked to comment on her private life, including the return to the Sunninghill Park house.

"We are happy with that and the children are happy with that. It is good harmony and it shows in the children," said the Duchess, who with daughters Beatrice,8, and Eugenie, 7, has since February been staying at the home the couple built after their 1986 wedding.
"We both believe in joint parenting and we both believe in the fact that we can put aside all our worries -- or all that we do -- so that we can be good parents for our two children," she added.
British tabloids last week reported speculation that Prince Andrew had allegedly lost patience and wanted the Duchess out after learning that she was going out on dates.
"We are in 1997 -- three years off the millenium," the Duchess commented.

The Duchess, who was divorced a year ago from Queen Elizabeth's second son Andrew, was in Poland visiting and raising funds for Children in Crisis, a charity she founded which runs a mountain resort and haven for sick children mostly from Poland's heavily-polluted southern industrial regions.

The Duchess has been taking part in advertisements and promotions in the United States, as well as working in journalism, to pay off debts. This prompted British tabloid newspapers to speculate that her move to Sunninghill was in part prompted by a need to save rent.

Asked how well she could find time for both the paid and charitable work, she said the fact she had raised four million sterling for Children in Crisis showed her dedication to the cause and to children in Poland was as great as to her everyday concerns.

The Duchess, in Poland for five days, appealed for local businesses to contribute more towards the centre, which offers severely sick children a chance to breathe fresh air and gain strength while within reach of sophisticated treatment.
